This update makes the launcher's panes more consistent, rebuilds widget editing, and brings presets, wallpapers, and optional tools into the launcher's download flow.
## A better widget pane
- Scroll through your widget board and find widgets through a searchable picker with previews. - Move widgets directly and resize them using four subtle corner handles. - See widgets resize while dragging, within the limits supported by each widget provider. - Settings and Widgets now stay expanded, with no floating-window controls. - Transparent pane backgrounds reveal the launcher through blur, including behind the status bar. Devices without blur support use dimming.
## Termux, connected through SSH
- The Termux pane now uses a local SSH connection, while Termux and tmux manage your shells and running jobs. - Keep the familiar split panes, workspace pages, launcher fonts, and colors. - Guided setup installs and configures the required Termux support. - Improved reconnection and session restoration when returning to the workspace. - Saved Termux Apps appear in launcher suggestions for quickly reopening your terminal tools. - Empty workspaces no longer show an unnecessary window chooser.
## Download what you want
- Browse and preview 21 curated terminal color presets with preset -market. - Downloaded presets are imported without changing your current appearance. Apply one when ready with preset -apply <saved-name>. - Preview optional wallpaper packs inside the launcher, confirm the download, and install them automatically. - Download and install the optional Qalculate engine directly from the calculator. - Browse and install native launcher modules with module -library.
## Settings and theme improvements
- Preview appearance changes before saving them. - Improved settings persistence and recovery of unfinished edits. - Better readability for transparent and low-contrast themes, plus fixes for cursor colors and panel borders. - More reliable preset imports from browsers and Android's file picker, with themed error screens and clearer recovery options. - Improved backup and interrupted-restore recovery, including preservation of older modules during upgrades.
## Everyday fixes
- Fixed basic calculator expressions showing preview unavailable. - Added haptic feedback to calculator keyboard controls. - The default-launcher prompt now appears after the preparation animation finishes. - Setup progress uses terminal glyphs. - Reduced repeated work when returning Home from another app. - Improved landscape pane alignment while respecting system and custom margins. - Improved IRC history refresh and added message deletion where supported by the server.
## Optional Private Space support
Enable the private command under Settings → Behaviour to access Android Private Space on supported devices.
This feature is off by default. It requires Android 15 or later and a compatible implementation of Android's standard Private Space APIs. Some manufacturer implementations, including the Vivo device tested during development, may authenticate successfully but still prevent app launching.
Authentication cancellation and retry handling have also been corrected.

## Hotfix #1 · Build 504
- Fixed the Settings preview crash when swiping between panes with transparent themes, including Kois. - Replaced the preview tabs with swipeable Status, Terminal, Music, Help and Calculator examples. Appearance drafts update the previews without saving or running actions. - Unlocked Private Space apps can now launch from typed app names. Use private -open <app name> to explicitly choose the private copy. - Fixed missing alphabetical headings in private -ls and repeated, out-of-order letter sections in the private app drawer. - Private app launching remains unavailable while locked or when Private Space support is disabled.
## Hotfix 2 · Build 505
- Notes now shares the pane frame, header, window controls and background blur used by Help and Calculator. - Notes actions sit inside the pane with simpler controls, improved spacing and room for the keyboard. - Use 10 Help home from any offline help article, topic list or command reference to jump directly to the main directory. - Updated offline topics for Notes, Settings previews, Private Space, the optional Qalculate engine and Termux SSH setup.
## Hotfix 3 · Build 506
- Notes dialogs, fields, cards and formatting popups now respect the selected border style, including borders off. - New-note and other Notes dialogs open at their final size without the entrance animation. - Added an optional toolbar gesture button: hold until it vibrates, drag up/down/left/right, then release. Return to the centre to cancel. - Configure gesture_button_enabled and gesture_up/down/left/right in toolbar.xml. Each direction accepts an app launcher name, alias or command; empty directions are disabled. For example, set gesture_up to notifications -open. - Restored swipe-up for the app drawer on non-scrolling launcher surfaces. Terminal output remains dedicated to scrolling.
## Hotfix 4 · Build 507
- Preserve legacy time_format lists for both status and output clocks when the replacement setting is missing. - Preserve existing current values and keep an original-file .pre-migration recovery copy before startup migrates settings. - Apply old status background, shadow, alignment and display-margin settings consistently across startup and presets. - Prefer current setting names over their old aliases. Reject conflicting duplicate settings before applying preset XML changes. - Keep valid opaque-black backgrounds and shadows instead of replacing them with transparency.
If an older version already deleted a clock format, restore it from a backup. This update cannot reconstruct previously deleted values.
## Hotfix 5 · Build 508
- Settings previews now reuse the current launcher status, terminal and module rendering, including the configured battery progress bar. - Swipe between Status, Terminal, Modules, Help, Calculator and ANSI preview cards. Help, Calculator and ANSI use illustrative samples. - Appearance drafts stay temporary until Save, and preview controls do not run commands or launch apps. - Choose already-imported frames from an inline list beneath each FRAME row, for one surface or all surfaces. Missing or corrupt frames are marked and unavailable for selection. Save Frame Settings applies the pending assignments. - Corrected the integration entry name to RE:TUI Keys Shortcuts.

Built-in modules include music, notifications, timer, calendar, reminder, notes, rss, and weather. Lua modules are edited locally in Re:T-UI, can render native buttons/layouts, and use module -new lua, module -edit, module -config, module -check, and module -approve. Termux modules execute shell scripts and render ::title, ::body, and ::suggest metadata. Suggestion-only Lua scripts remain helpers because they do not render a dock panel.

Home/app aliases and Termux-script aliases are separate scopes in alias.txt. alias -add saves a name and command, defaulting to home scope; place -a after -add for explicit home scope, or -s for a Termux script. Parameter expansion uses configurable marker/separator rules, not necessarily POSIX shell-function parsing. Use alias -ls to inspect mappings and alias -file to edit the file. Removal deletes only the chosen mapping.
Home aliases take precedence over built-in commands, so avoid conflicting names. Storing an alias changes configuration; invoking it executes its content. Save only code you trust. Script aliases require Termux, whose environment differs from the home prompt. Use termux -run or a module termux: source for Termux scripts.
shell explicitly dispatches the launcher's Android shell input with launcher access, not Termux's private environment. Bare unknown input reaches it only when shell_requires_prefix is false. A known launcher command that fails parsing is not silently run as shell.

Pinned shortcut handles begin with @ and retain package, shortcut ID and user-profile identity. They launch through Android LauncherApps, so the source app must still expose the shortcut. A label is not sufficient to restore a removed or disabled shortcut. Use shortcut -ls to discover published/pinned shortcuts and shortcut -use with a chosen handle/ID using completion. The Settings keyboard-shortcut panel is separate: it maps letters a-z to at most two app shortcuts each for the Re:TUI keyboard companion. Those mappings are token-authorized and pass icon content URIs to that package; installing the launcher alone does not install the keyboard. Neither shortcut feature is a shell alias. Use aliases for launcher command shortcuts, pinned handles for Android shortcuts, and keyboard mappings for companion-keyboard app launches.
App shortcuts require Android API 25 or later. shortcut -ls lists shortcuts and accepted pinned aliases; adding an app name narrows the list. shortcut -use accepts an ID, an index with an app name, or an @handle already accepted by the launcher. Check the list before running a shortcut: a shortcut may perform an app-specific action. The old -cp option is not implemented.

Remove deletes the hosted widget, not its source app. Long-press/edit exposes drag movement and edge-resize controls; outside touch cancels edit mode. Adding needs an installed widget provider and may open that app’s configuration screen. Widget content can depend on the provider app, Android access and network. These pane commands are not home launcher commands. The old widget command is retired and prints migration guidance for Lua modules. Use the native widgets pane for AppWidgets, module for dock Lua, and lua for app-like scripts. widget -add does not create an Android widget.

Hide only changes launcher visibility. Uninstall starts Android’s package deletion activity, including for hidden apps or a literal package fallback. tui -rm removes launcher device-admin status and asks Android to uninstall the launcher itself. Generated borders use the master enable_dashed_border switch plus per-surface enable/color overrides. Per-surface auto inherits the terminal border color; advanced AUTO colors inherit their role parents and are not explicit transparent colors. Zero dash gap makes a continuous enabled stroke; a positive gap makes dashed segments. Stroke/radius accessors clamp raw values, so extreme saved geometry is not an exact screen dimension. Unified-status border is separate.
Context-aware settings/config border writes refresh the running launcher in place. config -set persists changes; config -get reads stored values. If a change seems ineffective, check the surface override and custom frame before restarting.
Custom image frames take precedence over generated artwork; with a frame, generated fallback fill is transparent. Without a frame, fallback borders depend on border-enabled, Cyberdeck and dashed settings. Color options change fills/text, not custom-frame pixels. Disabling a surface/master dashed border does not delete its frame or disable every Cyberdeck border.

Tap the calculator input to position the cursor or select text. Function and square-root keys wrap selected text, or insert parentheses with the cursor inside. Backspace deletes the selection or previous character. ABC uses staggered QWERTY rows within the same keypad-height budget as 123, and long input scrolls horizontally. Expressions are limited to 1024 characters. Calculations have a timeout so a long-running expression cannot block the interface indefinitely. Cancel targets the active calculation and late results are ignored. The floating pane enforces minimum sizing for the input, hint and keypad; Calculator stays expanded in landscape. Larger fonts and a smaller screen can reduce the available floating resize range.

## Remember this device
On the default Re:TUI network, Remember this device authorizes a protected Android Keystore key after successful account authentication. Create account enables this choice by default and explains it before password entry; you can turn it off. Passwords are not saved. After enrollment is confirmed, opening IRC automatically reconnects and requests #retui.

Check your network and the chosen server, then use Reconnect or password Sign in. A rejected key or TLS failure does not silently downgrade authentication. ## Forget this device
Connection details offers Forget this device. While connected to the bound account it requests server revocation, waits for confirmation, then removes the local key and disconnects. ## Privacy and retention
TLS verifies and encrypts the connection, but messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Server operators can read channel and private messages. The server receives your connection address; nickname display and IP cloaking are not anonymity from the operator. Never share passwords or private recovery information in a channel.
The default network uses a one-week server-history policy with cleanup in batches, not instantaneous deletion. External networks have their own policies. Launcher has no persistent local transcript, background IRC service, push or offline replay in this version. Rotation retains conversations, but password entry cancels; leaving the pane disconnects. Process death does not preserve an unsent chat draft.
For default-network moderation, privacy or account-deletion requests, contact the developer privately. dvil is the configured moderator. Forget this device does not delete the server account or its history.

tasker runs a named Tasker task. It checks installed package, RUN_TASKS permission, Tasker enabled state and Allow External Access; task names are case-sensitive. A started message means broadcast dispatched, not necessarily task completed. Optional completion status waits at most 30 seconds. Incoming Tasker-plugin actions are separately controlled by Re:TUI integration enablement and support preset apply, theme color, module show/refresh/text, terminal output and Space switch. Termux/script callbacks use exported com.dvil.tui_renewed.RETUI_CALLBACK with a locally generated token. retuitoken -status reports enabled/token-present without printing the token. -show and -on enable callbacks and display/copy the token; -rotate creates and displays/copies a replacement. -off disables callback authorization. Keep tokens out of screenshots, shared behavior text and public docs. Rotate invalidates old callbacks; personal backup includes callback auth preferences. Callbacks only support output, notify (terminal output, not Android push) and module_set/module text. They do not implement arbitrary authenticated exec. The Re:TUI Tasker-integration switch gates incoming plugin actions, not the outbound tasker command. Running a task can change device state or send data according to that task; inspect it in Tasker first.
Task names may be quoted, optionally after -run; permanent Tasker suggestions execute when tapped. retui-token is a public alias for retuitoken. Update integrations after token rotation.
The Re:T-UI Tasker plug-in offers apply preset, set theme, show/refresh/update module, terminal output and switch Space. It shows fields for the selected action, including a custom preset/Space name or Tasker variable where supported. These actions can change live launcher state. The plug-in reports a failed action rather than treating it as successful. Back in plug-in configuration attempts to save; it is not an unconditional discard action. Tasker must already be installed with the required permissions and setup.

## Approve the matching helper
Opening the Termux workspace checks compatibility with the helper bundled in this APK. Update now installs that matching helper through Termux and reconnects the bridge. Later installs nothing. Inside the workspace, :update reopens the prompt. There is no silent update or background download from a changing Git branch.
The update replaces the normal helper path, including a custom helper there, only after approval. It verifies decoded bytes with SHA-256 and atomically replaces the file. Installation failures attempt rollback; the previous helper is retained at $PREFIX/share/retui/retui.previous. Existing shells, running jobs and workspace layout are kept. Only bridge connections restart.
## Setup is separate
Termux must already be installed, Launcher must have command permission, and allow-external-apps must be enabled in Termux by the user. If tmux or socat is missing, install them in Termux with pkg install tmux socat. The prompt offers permission, Termux and setup-guide actions; it does not silently grant access or install dependencies.
## If an update fails
Check the displayed error and prerequisites before retrying. A command with no reply may still finish inside Termux; Launcher does not automatically replay the installation. Leaving Launcher does not cancel a command already dispatched to Termux.
A lock prevents concurrent replacements. After an interrupted update, retry may report a running or interrupted lock. Launcher never deletes unknown locks automatically. Open the setup guide, inspect $PREFIX/share/retui/.update-lock only after checking that no updater is running, and retain the previous helper if recovery is needed. Never kill the tmux server as a routine update fix.

## Workspace pages and tiles
Single, Top-bottom and Left-right choose the visible layout, with at most two tiles targeting independent tmux windows. Tap a tile to choose where keyboard input goes. Add asks whether to replace a tile, split the page or create a new page; replacing a view does not kill its old shell.

timer accepts s/m/h unit segments such as 5m or 1h30m. Only one timer runs; starting a second prompts whether to add time, while -add explicitly extends it (or starts a new timer if none is active). -status is read-only and -stop cancels. Bare timer shows help, not a duration picker. Stopwatch starts on bare command, stops/continues and resets through its own options; it is separate from countdown. Pomodoro uses configured focus/break durations (defaults 25/5 minutes) over four cycles and persists phase/deadline. A supplied goal starts; bare command opens setup. Dystopia is optional and off by default. When enabled, early stop can spend virtual credits or require emergency Breach. Lockdown is its related launcher focus overlay and does not hard-block other Android apps or act as device policy. Timer and stopwatch state is held in memory and can be lost when the launcher process ends. Pomodoro and Lockdown save their state, but saved state is not an alarm-delivery guarantee. Starting, extending, stopping or resetting a timer or focus session changes state; -status only reports it.

webhook -add saves a name, destination URL and body template in webhooks.xml. Invoking a named webhook renders its arguments and dispatches an asynchronous HTTP POST. Nonempty arguments are saved to recent history before dispatch, including when the request later fails; up to five entries per webhook feed suggestions. JSON templates substitute within parsed values to preserve escaping; plain-text templates use simpler substitution. Inspect the endpoint and template before invoking one. Requests can disclose arguments or trigger remote actions. A dispatched request or HTTP response does not prove the remote service performed the action you intended. Personal backups can include webhook definitions and history; treat those archives as private. webhook -ls sends no request, but prints both names and URLs. A URL may contain a secret token: do not share its terminal output or screenshots without checking. Outbound webhooks are separate from inbound token-authorized callbacks.
